document_example.body:
Knowledge Pipeline v1

CPU-first · Evidence-driven · Formally verifiable · Private by design

Status: Engineering design and implementation brief. All timing and accuracy thresholds labeled *target* are unvalidated until benchmarked.

Executive decision

Build a deterministic Rust processing engine that converts text from any authorized online or offline source into compact, classified, source-backed semantic observations. Use inexpensive CPU classifiers for the bulk of categorization, incrementally connect observations to a modest seeded ontology, and reserve local non-frontier AI for select ambiguity, ontology arbitration, and evidence-grounded explanation.

The product has three distinct systems:

1. Extract: Rust/CPU real-time structural and semantic processing. 2. Learn: CPU graph alignment, evidence reconciliation, and conservative ontology evolution. 3. Educate: Indexed retrieval, deterministic answer planning, and selective local AI explanation.

Don't use a full AMR parser in the synchronous path. Borrow its semantic ideas (actors, roles, predicates, negation, modality, attribution) and represent them compactly. Preserve uncertain interpretations rather than asserting unsupported facts.

1. Operational architecture

Synchronous: G0–G3 and journal append. Asynchronous: G4–G5, ontology change proposals, and explanations. No graph database or LLM is required to classify an incoming item.

The source material remains in the owner's authorized envelope. Access policies apply to derived observations and explanations as well as to original documents. Shared public concept definitions must not expose private tenant evidence.

2. Stage gates and concrete techniques

Gate | Default CPU algorithm | Output | When to escalate | ---|---|---|---| G0 — Normalize | Source adapters, hashes, language heuristics, source/permission metadata | Resident text and validated provenance | Unsupported format/language | G1 — Scan | SIMD/bit masks, precompiled finite-state machines | Word/span offsets, clause cues, entity candidates | Unsupported structure; preserve raw source | G2 — Semantic solver | Bounded predicate-role templates, local weighted constraints | Subject/predicate/object fragments and qualifiers | Ambiguous role assignment | G3a — Sparse classify | Hashed character/word n-grams + logistic regression or fastText-like baseline | Multi-label Domains/Areas, content function, conditions | Scores fail calibrated gate | G3b — Deeper CPU classify | Optional quantized compact encoder with shared heads | Improved difficult labels | Abstain if still uncertain | G4 — Align | Stable IDs, inverted indexes, typed relation matching | Linked observations, evidence sets, conflicts | Identity or contradiction unresolved | G5 — Evolve | Provisional residual clusters, novelty and promotion checks | Candidate or approved ontology revisions | Material, unresolved structural decision | G6 — Educate | Indexed retrieval, claim/evidence selection, templates; optional local AI | Short answers with sources and adjacent concepts | Complex narrative synthesis |

Crucial: Confident classification of an Area must never skip G2 relationship extraction. Document classification and local semantic extraction serve different purposes. G3b should be invoked per unresolved task/head, not necessarily for every unresolved document.

3. Established methods versus proposed components

Method | Status | Application | ---|---|---| Hashed n-gram logistic regression / fastText | Established research and engineering approach | Fast CPU multilabel classification | Weak supervision (Snorkel-style labeling functions) | Established research approach | Build training labels from rules, with human calibration | DenStream-style data-stream clustering | Established research approach | Compare as a method for provisional unaligned concepts | ADWIN drift detection | Established research approach | Monitor changes in data/class distributions | W3C PROV-O | Published provenance standard | Model source, activity, and derivation | Lean 4 | Established proof assistant | Prove model-level invariants and transition rules | Bounded predicate-role Rust solver | Proposed design | Extract useful subset of AMR-like semantics at low latency | Concept promotion scoring/rules | Proposed design | Controlled ontology growth; requires calibration | 1 ms extraction for 10 MiB | Stretch target, not measured | Experiment after scan floor and accuracy have been established |

Useful starting references:

Joulin et al., *Bag of Tricks for Efficient Text Classification* (fastText): https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.01759 Ratner et al., *Snorkel: Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision*: https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.10160 Cao et al., *Density-Based Clustering over an Evolving Data Stream* (DenStream): https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611972757.29 Bifet and Gavaldà, *Learning from Time-Changing Data with Adaptive Windowing* (ADWIN): https://doi.org/10.1137/1.9781611972771.42 W3C PROV-O: https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/ Lean 4 documentation: https://lean-lang.org/documentation/

These references support the individual techniques, not an assertion that the full proposed architecture is already scientifically validated.

4. Classification cascade

Classifier heads:

Head | Output | Semantics | ---|---|---| Domain | Broad sectors | Multilabel | Area | Seeded and accepted ontology Areas | Multilabel | Content function | Report, opinion, prediction, request, decision, etc. | Potentially multilabel | Conditions | Rising, falling, delayed, disrupted, expanded, etc. | Multilabel, with direction | Capability | Known capability IDs and candidate associations | Multilabel | Novelty | Known / emerging / unsupported | Routing signal, never automatic ontology invention |

For sparse feature vector `x` and label `j`:

\[ z_j = b_j + \sum_{i\in active(x)} w_{ji} x_i \]

Predicted probabilities need calibration; raw dot products or embedding similarity are not calibrated confidence. Select thresholds on a held-out validation set. The operating objective is to minimize expected CPU cost subject to target error and coverage constraints. If the data distribution drifts, re-evaluate those calibrations.

Start with a hashed n-gram linear model, benchmark against an existing compact CPU encoder, and retain the encoder only where it delivers measurable gain. If the already trained shared encoder meets the total latency budget, compare two deployments: encoder-on-every-item versus sparse-first selective escalation. Measure throughput and per-head accuracy.

5. Semantic data contract

Every processed source becomes compact observations. Preserve actor/object spans, predicate IDs, uncertainty, factuality, and original evidence offsets. A proposed high-level schema:

The production hot path should use packed IDs, borrowed slices, preallocated buffers, and explicit capacity bounds rather than heap-allocating the above vectors per token.

A separate provenance record includes source owner, source path/URL, timestamps, hash, permission policy, language, transformation history, and extraction version. Keep identity, factual accuracy, and authorization as separate attributes.

6. Rust pipeline sketch

Execution properties: Hot-load rule tables, weights and buffers before the clock; reuse spotter features; never require a recognized name from a catalog; keep unknown or contradictory labels; persist before asynchronous graph materialization. Journal append and associated allocations should be separately measured if testing an in-memory extraction-only timing target.

7. End-to-end sequence

8. Knowledge model: Observation, assertion, concept

Keep these distinct:

1. Observation: Source says *Acme announced a factory expansion*. Immutable, provenance-backed, possibly uncertain. 2. Assertion: *Acme plans production expansion*. Supported by one or more observations; retains attribution, time and polarity. 3. Ontology concept: *Manufacturing capacity expansion*. Reusable, independent of Acme.

An event is not automatically a taxonomy node. A document may be routed to an existing Area without creating a new Area. Cross-document identity matching must distinguish *same name* from *same entity*.

The diagram represents conceptual *association*, not data declassification. Private evidence cannot be retrieved from public-facing answers, even if associated with a shared capability.

Deterministic alignment

Find candidate assertions through tenant-scoped indexed lookups:

\[ Candidates(f)=I_{entity}(f)\cup I_{predicate}(f)\cup I_{area}(f) \]

Score candidates using entity compatibility, predicates, semantic roles, time and context. This is a candidate design, not a proven accuracy metric:

\[ Match(f,k)=w_eE+w_pP+w_rR+w_tT+w_cC \]

Evaluate the weights on labeled same-assertion/nonmatch pairs. Attach independent evidence where appropriate; retain incompatible assertions with explicit conflict edges rather than overwriting them.

9. Dynamic ontology design

Seed a small, versioned ontology: Domains → Areas → optional Subareas → Capabilities. Underlying storage is a typed directed graph, not a single-parent tree. A Capability may be reused across Areas without duplication.

Two independent forms of growth:

Knowledge depth: More evidence, mechanisms, exceptions, time trends and understanding within existing concepts. Ontology refinement: A truly useful new specialization, capability, cross-link, split or merge.

Run novelty/discovery predominantly on residual observations that do not align satisfactorily with existing concepts. Compare a straightforward bounded micro-cluster baseline with DenStream-style clustering. Avoid reclustering the entire world on every document.

Promotion checks:

Independent evidence diversity (deduplicate syndication and replay). Semantic coherence and recurring relation structure. Distinctiveness from current ontology nodes. Reusability beyond a short-lived event. Explanatory gain: better organizing/retrieving knowledge. Valid typed relationships and preserved history.

Automated promotion requires a human-reviewed evaluation regime; otherwise keep the node provisional. A frequently reported unsupported claim may form a *topic*, but it must not be asserted as true.

Typed relations and invariants:

Relation | Meaning | Rule | ---|---|---| `is_a` | Specializes concept | Acyclic; can infer transitive ancestry | `part_of` | Component relationship | Not interchangeable with `is_a` | `enables` | Functional link | Requires evidence | `requires` | Dependency | Cycles may be valid | `related_to` | Adjacent/tangential | Not necessarily transitive | `same_as` | Canonical identity | Strong identity evidence needed | `supported_by` | Evidence provenance | Authorized valid reference | `contradicts` | Conflicting claims | Preserve both claims |

10. Macro Pulse and educator

An Area/Capability answer should quickly explain:

What it is: One- or two-sentence common understanding. What is changing: Dated developments and trends. Why it matters: The actual supporting relationships and dependencies. What is known: Supported claims and their provenance. What remains uncertain: Gaps, contradictions, stale coverage. Adjacent Areas: Tangential concepts a user might drill into next.

Suggested pulse dimensions (not a single aggregated certainty number):

\[ Pulse(a,t)=(V,\Delta V,N,C,U) \]

`V` independent observation volume; `ΔV` change against baseline; `N` novelty; `C` conflict; `U` unresolved uncertainty. Also report coverage and freshness independently from evidence confidence.

Generate answers by selecting authorized evidence and claims first, then optionally use local AI to narrate them. Never let the LLM introduce unsupported statements. A useful objective is to maximize relevance and support while penalizing redundancy and unsupported claims, constrained by evidence visibility. This objective is a design hypothesis, not a Lean theorem about factual truth.

11. Lean 4 verification boundaries

Lean should verify the behavior of the reference kernel and ontology update rules, not run inside the per-document hot path. Formal proof of a Lean model does not automatically prove arbitrary optimized Rust code: compare the reference model against Rust via differential, property-based and generated tests; a fully verified implementation correspondence would require additional work.

Evidence set algebra

Evidence membership as union has the useful associative, commutative, idempotent shape. Actual evidence IDs must distinguish independent corroboration from replay/syndication; that assignment is not proved by union alone.

Source span validity

Proof roadmap

Phase | Prove | Verify empirically | ---|---|---| P0 | Bounds/valid references | Correct source/text offset mapping | P1 | Evidence merge associativity, commutativity, idempotence | Replay vs syndicated source identity | P2 | Stream chunk invariance under stated state/finalization semantics | Different chunk sizes and latency | P3 | Role/type constraints and preserved qualifiers | Extraction precision and recall | P4 | `is_a` acyclicity and well-typed graph changes | Semantic suitability of associations | P5 | Evidence retention and lineage across splits/merges | Quality of concept evolution | P6 | Optimized solver and reference model produce equivalent normalized output | Performance, memory, compiler/runtime behavior |

Streaming property to target: processing `x ++ y` as one input gives the same canonical fragments as processing `x`, carrying forward bounded state, then `y`, and finalizing. The state bound must account for long spans and the supported language grammar.

12. Reproducible test corpus

Test | Example | Expected behavior | ---|---|---| T01 | New battery technology improves grid storage | Energy and Technology classification | T02 | Veltrix acquired Calden Robotics | Unseen candidate entities and acquisition edge | T03 | Analysts expect electricity prices to rise | Prediction, not confirmed rise | T04 | Company denies plans to close factory | Denial/negation maintained | T05 | Liquid cooling reduces server heat | Thermal management capability | T06 | Hospitals deploy AI diagnostic hardware | Cross-domain links | T07 | Same story syndicated by 20 sources | Distinct citations but not 20 independent observations | T08 | Repeated references to unknown technology | Provisional concept rather than instant promotion | T09 | Private document aligns with public story | No private evidence leakage | T10 | Same bytes in 1 KiB, 64 KiB, whole-file chunks | Identical canonical output |

Also include hard negatives: incomplete sentences, quotation boundaries, weak context, non-English input, unknown predicates, misleading capitalization, dense entity text, entity coreference, multiword expressions, contradictory reports. Synthetic tests verify functional plumbing; use a held-out human-reviewed corpus for true accuracy and unseen-entity generalization.

13. CPU classifier training and rollout

Use independent group splits by source/event/time where appropriate, so syndicated copies of the same story do not appear in both train and test. Maintain human-reviewed ground truth. Weak labels and LLM labels are training inputs, not independent validation truth. Benchmark linear-first escalation against encoder-every-item using equal hardware and workloads.

14. Release gates and performance plan

Metric | Acceptance criterion / target | ---|---| Provenance | 100% of accepted observations have valid source pointers | Tenant access | No unauthorized disclosure in exhaustive policy test scenarios | Stream invariance | Identical normalized output for supported chunk schedules | Replay safety | No duplicate evidence membership on replay | Structural correctness | Committed ontology changes satisfy typed graph invariants | Classification | Per-head precision, recall, coverage, calibration and abstention | Open-world semantic extraction | Strict entity-span F1 and relation F1, including unseen names | AI utilization | Escalations / 1,000 items, reason, token and compute cost | Latency | p50/p95/p99 per stage; news items and dense 10 MiB inputs | Ontology | Promotion precision, duplicate concepts, unsupported merges |

Workload | Initial performance objective | ---|---| Resident 10 MiB byte scan | Investigate 1 ms stretch floor | Resident 10 MiB fused semantic solver | Compare against existing sub-20 ms NER | Sparse classifier per short news item | Sub-millisecond *inference-only* target; measure | Compact CPU encoder per short news item | Existing sub-50 ms end-to-end classification goal | Graph alignment | Async bounded candidate search | Ontology changes | Batch and version; never block intake |

The in-memory 10 MiB/1 ms goal corresponds to ~10.5 GB/s effective traversal. It is an aggressive stretch, particularly for actual relation inference on one core. Separate scan cost, candidate cost, semantic solver cost, output cost, journal cost, and total steady-state system throughput. No hot-load/cold-start time should enter the extraction benchmark, but production latency should also measure those operational components independently.

15. Suggested repository structure

16. Implementation checklist

[ ] 1. Benchmark baseline: Profile spotter/NER, 10 MiB scan floor, linear classifier and existing CPU encoder. Record core, candidate density, instruction and cache metrics, latency. [ ] 2. Canonical observation contract: Define valid spans, source IDs, provenance, qualifiers, evidence deduplication and model/ontology versions. [ ] 3. Sparse CPU classifier: Train hashed n-gram models for Domain, Area, content function and conditions. Calibrate independently; compare encoder baseline. [ ] 4. Fused predicate-role solver: Reuse spot map; implement bounded rules, exact source offsets, negation/modality/attribution. [ ] 5. Deterministic knowledge alignment: Tenant-scoped indexes, assertion matching, conflicting evidence, stable IDs, async journal consumer. [ ] 6. Dynamic ontology: Residual clustering, validated promotion, splitting/merging, lineage and versioning. [ ] 7. Macro Pulse and educator: Evidence-backed answers, pulse metrics, missing knowledge, adjacent capability suggestions; local AI only as needed.

17. Decisions and explicit assumptions

1. Text-first processing. Voice/video must first be transcribed; images are out of scope for the core knowledge pipeline. 2. Private envelopes. Every derived observation remains scoped to authorized principals; public conceptual vocabulary is allowed, not unauthorized content sharing. 3. Existing Rust primitives. Prefer reusing the current fused spot map and deterministic NER work rather than creating a new tokenizer/parser. 4. No full AMR on intake. Use minimal AMR-inspired roles/predicates/context, not complete semantic graph parsing. 5. CPU first. Small trainable classifiers are allowed. Local non-frontier AI is an exceptional, budgeted component. 6. Small seeded ontology. Domains, Areas, optional subareas, Capabilities and shared relations; progressively refine rather than learning everything from zero. 7. Separation of concerns. Extraction accuracy, evidence truthfulness, graph structural invariants, and user-facing explanation quality are independently evaluated. 8. Proofs are bounded. Lean proves model correctness under its stated assumptions, not classifier generalization or hardware execution time. 9. Durability boundary. Journal first; graph alignment and ontology evolution consume asynchronously, with replay-safe processing. 10. Macro Pulse. Prioritize answers, confidence dimensions, novelty and adjacent concepts over a wiki dump.

Final recommendation

The first two implementation experiments should run in parallel: (a) sparse CPU classifier versus the existing shared encoder on identical data, and (b) a bounded predicate-role solver fused with the existing Rust spot map. Meanwhile, formally specify the semantic observation contract and evidence merge semantics in Lean 4. Those results decide where computational complexity and verification effort will deliver genuine value.

articles.title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records

contract.title: More NHS staff sacked over attacks victims' records
contract.description: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust says a new system will be brought in to protect records.
contract.snapshot: Further members of staff have been sacked by an NHS trust for inappropriately accessing medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims. Nottingham students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death
contract.body: Further members of staff have been sacked by an NHS trust for inappropriately accessing medical records of the Nottingham attacks victims. Nottingham students Barnaby Webber and Grace O'Malley-Kumar, and grandfather Ian Coates, were stabbed to death on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, who was diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020. In May, Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust confirmed it had dismissed 11 members of staff and, in an update on Friday, said a total of 15 people had now been sacked as part of its investigation. Dr Sanjoy Kumar, Grace's father, said: "I am appalled, it's time to get a handle on these failures." He added: "Clearly, the way that the highest confidential data, which is medical data, is being looked at by voyeuristic people in the NHS is disgraceful." Dr Manjeet Shehmar, medical director at NUH, said: "There is simply no excuse for accessing the records of a patient without a legitimate reason and I hope this sends a really clear message – we will investigate and we will take action. "To lose a loved one in the way that the families of Ian, Grace and Barnaby have is heartbreaking enough. "I am so sorry that they have had this further compounded by the actions of these staff members." As well as the dismissals, NUH said 15 final written warnings and two first written warnings have also been issued in total. Two cases were found to have no case to answer and no action was taken. The trust said action had been taken against "doctors, nurses, registered healthcare professionals and other staff" and that independent regulators such as the Nursing and Midwifery Council and General Medical Council, the Information Commissioner's Office, and Nottinghamshire Police had been informed. A new system, currently under testing, is being implemented to protect patient records in future and alert the trust of potential breaches. A Your Responsibility, Your Actions, Their Privacy campaign has also been carried out to educate staff about data protection and the "serious consequences" of not following the rules, it added. Shehmar said: "We will continue to investigate inappropriate access to these records and take action as and where necessary. "Alongside this, we are doing all we can to educate our staff on appropriate access and how to keep the records of our patients safe. We are also introducing a new system which acts to detect possible data breaches. "While the actions of these staff members are disappointing, we know that this represents a small number of our wider workforce. "We know staff across the trust are listening, learning and doing what they can to ensure that only lawful and justified access takes place in our hospitals." NUH said investigations were continuing, including into inappropriate access of the files of the surviving victims of the attacks - Wayne Birkett, Sharon Miller and Marcin Gawronski. The first dismissals were made public amid a statutory public inquiry examining the lead-up to the attacks and decisions and actions taken in the aftermath. The judge-led Nottingham Inquiry, external heard from 164 witnesses during 14 weeks of harrowing evidence between February and June 2026, as well as two days of closing statements from core participants in September. The findings of the inquiry, which is being led by retired senior judge Deborah Taylor KC, will be published by May 2027. The hearings scrutinised authorities that had interactions with Calocane in the years before the attacks, laying bare failures and missed opportunities by agencies, including the NHS and police. The inquiry heard Calocane had been sectioned four times under the Mental Health Act and had a history of police interactions linked to violent incidents before the killings. Calocane is serving an indefinite hospital order, after pleading guilty to manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility, due to his paranoid schizophrenia, in January 2024. NUH is among a number of organisations in which staff inappropriately viewed records or information related to the fatal attacks. In December 2024, an investigation opened into allegations Ministry of Justice (MoJ) staff illegally accessed computer files related to the Nottingham attacks. The public inquiry has since heard court workers also inappropriately accessed information about the case in January 2024. Amy Holmes, the interim director general for the chief operating group of the Ministry of Justice (MoJ), told the inquiry she could not detail what information was accessed due to the ongoing police investigation. The inquiry also heard seven probation service officers were identified as having accessed the information. HM Prison and Probation Service found four of those officers accessed files legitimately, but three did not have a legitimate reason to do so. However, it was deemed by the probation service and the Ministry of Justice's data protection unit that the breaches were not serious enough to warrant further action. Footage and images related to the attacks were also viewed numerous times by Nottinghamshire Police staff without a legitimate policing purpose. The force confirmed it would carry out an audit of how many times the information was viewed and whether it was appropriate, following a complaint by Barnaby's mother, Emma Webber, in March. ## Get in touch Tell us which stories we should cover in Nottingham *Listen to BBC Radio Nottingham on Sounds and follow BBC Nottingham on Facebook*, external*, on X*, external*, or on Instagram*, external*. articles.title: What kind of winter is coming? NOAA's outlook offers clues for New England

contract.title: What kind of winter is coming? NOAA's outlook offers clues for New England
contract.description: Boston, MA – February 24: On the hills overlooking Dorchester Bay, shovelers push and carry snow to liberate their cars on February 24, 2026, the day after a massive blizzard hit the region. (Photo by Stan Grossfeld/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)

contract.body: El Niño will play a major role in the winter ahead. The warmer than normal sea surface temperatures will set up the jet stream or “storm track” over the southern tier of the country. This storm track is for precipitation, not necessarily snow, as temperatures will be above normal for much of the country. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration released its U.S. Winter Outlook on Thursday, including key details on what we can expect here in New England. The winter outlook outlines the conveyer belt for moisture and weather systems to travel across the country. And this El Nino will likely favor a storm track that begins over California, travels across the southern tier of the country and pushes the low pressure systems somewhere between the southeast and mid Atlantic. “As we know from decades of observations, a very strong El Nino will likely bring a southward and eastward shift to the jet stream for the contiguous U.S., which tilts the odds toward stormier weather across the South,” said Ken Graham, director of NOAA’s National Weather Service. “While higher chances of rain and snow may bring relief to drought-afflicted areas, too much precipitation on dry soil can fuel destructive flash floods and mudslides. Now is the time for communities and individuals to plan ahead for the upcoming winter.” Here’s a closer look at what to expect this winter here in New England: ## Temperature outlook Warmer than normal temperatures expected for New England for the December through February timeframe. Warmer than normal temperatures bring a greater likelihood of messy winter systems with a larger chance for wintry rain, snow mix and ice. But there will still be cold snaps, and when this colder air meets with winter systems, snow accumulations are still very much possible. ## Precipitation outlook Wetter than normal conditions possible across southern New England. This is still a location with a bit of uncertainty. But with the storm track setting up across the south, there’s a chance that sets the stage for nor’easters to move up the coast. No promises, but under the right circumstances, low pressure systems that exit over the southeast or mid Atlantic can then be steered north along the East Coast, giving a classic nor’easter set up. ## Drought outlook Drought relief is expected across much of the country, including parts of New England. Massachusetts, Connecticut, Rhode Island and southern New Hampshire and Vermont are forecast to remain drought-free, while Maine and northern parts of New Hampshire and Vermont could see drought conditions improve or disappear. This will be much different than previous seasons where we continuously saw rain deficits which we are still making up for. NOAA’s seasonal outlook does not project seasonal snowfall totals, as snow forecasts are generally not predictable more than a week in advance. The outlook is updated monthly, and the next one will be released on Nov. 19.

contract.title: Trump defends Russia sanctions waivers, accuses Zelenskyy of 'prolonging war'
contract.description: US President Donald Trump again accused Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. The remarks come amid renewed tensions over US policy toward Moscow including waiving some sanctions.
contract.snapshot: Trump accuses Zelenskyy of 'prolonging war' October 19, 2026 US President Donald Trumpon Sunday defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. "My decision on
contract.body: Trump accuses Zelenskyy of 'prolonging war' October 19, 2026 US President Donald Trumpon Sunday defended his decision to waive some sanctions on Russia, accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of not wanting to end the war. "My decision on Russia is a very simple one. I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table," Trump wrote on Truth Social. "Zelenskyy doesn't care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him, and that Crooked Joe Biden gave him in the past, he doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did," he added. Trump signed an executive order late Friday waiving broad new sanctions mandated by legislation named for the late US Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Ukraine's defense. He has also temporarily waived sanctions on Russian diesel, allowing supplies to flow into global markets in a bid to lower fuel prices ahead of US midterm elections on November 3. ## Trump links Russia sanctions waiver to fuel prices ahead of midterms Opinion polls suggest that Republicans could face significant losses in the election, as voters voice growing frustration over fuel prices that have surged since the Iran war began in late February. Most economists believe the suspension of congressionally approved sanctions on Russia and the diesel deal with the Kremlin will do little to lower US fuel prices. Trump also repeated his claim that Ukraine was targeting Russian refineries to hurt Republicans ahead of the midterm election. The move drew a sharp response from Kyiv and its allies, further straining relations between Trump and Zelenskyy. ## Zelenskyy warns Ukraine cannot prevail if US backs Russia Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned Sunday that Ukraine would lose its defensive battle against Russia if the United States switched sides and supported Moscow. "If the United States will take the side of Russia, of course we will not prevail," Zelenskyy told NBC's 'Meet the Press' calling a withdrawal of US support "a historic mistake and big tragedy." He said Washington had resumed sharing intelligence after it was "blocked for some period of time," adding that Ukraine had missed critical intelligence on ballistic missile attacks for three days. Zelenskyy also criticized US restrictions affecting Ukraine's war effort, saying, "We are strategic partners," but "we cannot applaud when someone turns against Ukraine." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Trump's suspension of new sanctions on Russia, saying Trump wanted to assess their impact on the global and US economies. ## Zelenskyy speaks to US envoys as Trump renews criticism Volodymyr Zelenskyy spoke to US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner as Russia and Ukraine attacked each other's energy infrastructure, leaving thousands without power in Ukraine and setting an oil refinery ablaze near Saint Petersburg. After the talks, Zelenskyy said "a lot depends" on the US position, adding that "this war must be brought to an end." Ukraine was ready to work "constructively" and "honestly," he said, calling for the same approach from its European and US partners. Zelenskyy said he also discussed deliveries of US Patriot air defense systems as Kyiv struggles to counter Russian missiles. A US-led push to end the war has yet to yield a breakthrough, with Trump expressing frustration at both Zelenskyy and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Zelenskyy accused Moscow of violating Trump's "energy ceasefire" 76 times and warned Russia planned to deprive Ukrainians of heat and electricity before winter. Russian strikes left "tens of thousands" without power, he said, while Ukrainian officials reported three deaths. Ukraine launched drones at Putin's hometown of Saint Petersburg late Sunday, setting an oil refinery ablaze and killing one person, Moscow said. *Edited by: Dmytro Hubenko* *If you rely on our team for trusted reporting, please take a moment to select us as your Preferred Source on Google, so you'll always see our verified news first.*

definitions: Stated fact
An amount, date, name or who-did-what link that is in the text, with the exact words and what it attaches to. 'Stated' does not mean true.
Validator
A fixed check against the text: the words are really there, the value reads back, it attaches to a noun or verb, and it sits inside one sentence.
Keyword rule
A hand-written list of words for one kind. It fires if any word is in the story, e.g. civil unrest: protest, riot, unrest, demonstrat, clashes, tear gas, curfew, looting, uprising, coup.
Sparse head
A small statistical model that counts words, word pairs and letter patterns and learned yes or no for one kind from Sonnet's labels.
Encoder head
A small neural network turns the story's first 64 word-pieces into 1,024 numbers; a simple model on those numbers learned yes or no for one kind from Sonnet's labels.
Held-out
Stories never used to train a model or to set its thresholds. Here: 2,082 of 20,790 labelled stories (16,627 train, 2,081 set thresholds).
Sonnet's labels
What Claude Sonnet wrote for each story. A model's opinion, not truth. The heads above learned from it, so matching it is partly circular.
Outside human labels
Labels made by people for other projects (MN-DS topics, CheckThat fact versus opinion, MAVEN-FACT events). The only kind of check that can tell us a model is right.
Match score (z)
How unusually close an open phrase is in meaning to a vocabulary entry, in standard deviations above a background of other phrases. A similarity estimate, not a probability.
F1
One number out of 1 that balances finding the real cases against calling wrong ones; 1 is perfect.
Balanced accuracy
The average of the share of each class found, so a common class cannot hide a missed rare one.
